title: Camping at home
setting: Friday evening in the flat Kenta and Sora share. Kenta has spent a month planning a weekend camping trip for the two of them, and Sora, who dropped out last time when work came up, has sworn he's coming. Then a typhoon turns up in the news.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, ashita no kyanpu, honto ni daijoubu? kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamotte yo.
lines.ja: ソラ、明日のキャンプ、ほんとに大丈夫？今度はちゃんと約束守ってよ。
lines.kana: そら、あしたのきゃんぷ、ほんとにだいじょうぶ？こんどはちゃんとやくそくまもってよ。
lines.english: Sora, are you really OK for tomorrow's camping? Keep your promise this time, properly.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daijoubu da tte. mae wa kyuu ni shigoto haitchatta dake da yo. yakusoku wa mamoru yo.
lines.ja: 大丈夫だって。前は急に仕事入っちゃっただけだよ。約束は守るよ。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶだって。まえはきゅうにしごとはいっちゃっただけだよ。やくそくはまもるよ。
lines.english: I told you, it's fine. Last time work just came up out of nowhere. I'll keep my promise.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nara ii kedo. sengetsu kara keikaku tateteta n da kara ne.
lines.ja: ならいいけど。先月から計画立ててたんだからね。
lines.kana: ならいいけど。せんげつからけいかくたててたんだからね。
lines.english: Good, then. I've been planning this since last month, you know.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: shitteru yo. a, chotto kore mite. ashita, taifuu kuru tte.
lines.ja: 知ってるよ。あ、ちょっとこれ見て。明日、台風来るって。
lines.kana: しってるよ。あ、ちょっとこれみて。あした、たいふうくるって。
lines.english: I know. Oh, look at this. They say a typhoon's coming tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: e, uso. demo, mada wakannai yo ne. toriaezu ashita no asa made yousu miyou.
lines.ja: え、うそ。でも、まだわかんないよね。とりあえず明日の朝まで様子見よう。
lines.kana: え、うそ。でも、まだわかんないよね。とりあえずあしたのあさまでようすみよう。
lines.english: What, no way. But we can't tell yet, right? Let's just wait and see till tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. a, mite. nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai, mou chuushi ni natta tte.
lines.ja: うん。あ、見て。日曜日のサッカーの試合、もう中止になったって。
lines.kana: うん。あ、みて。にちようびのさっかーのしあい、もうちゅうしになったって。
lines.english: Yeah. Oh, look. Sunday's football match has already been called off.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: maji de? a, kyanpujou kara meeru da.
lines.ja: マジで？あ、キャンプ場からメールだ。
lines.kana: まじで？あ、きゃんぷじょうからめーるだ。
lines.english: Seriously? Oh, there's an email from the campsite.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: dame da. taifuu de, kyanpu chuushi ni natta. yoyaku mo kyanseru shinakya.
lines.ja: だめだ。台風で、キャンプ中止になった。予約もキャンセルしなきゃ。
lines.kana: だめだ。たいふうで、きゃんぷちゅうしになった。よやくもきゃんせるしなきゃ。
lines.english: No good. The camping's been called off because of the typhoon. I'll have to cancel the booking too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: zannen. ashita made yousu miru hitsuyou mo nakatta ne.
lines.ja: 残念。明日まで様子見る必要もなかったね。
lines.kana: ざんねん。あしたまでようすみるひつようもなかったね。
lines.english: Too bad. Guess we didn't even need to wait and see till tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: haa, sekkaku keikaku tateta noni naa.
lines.ja: はあ、せっかく計画立てたのになあ。
lines.kana: はあ、せっかくけいかくたてたのになあ。
lines.english: Sigh. After all the trouble I went to planning it.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa sa, uchi de kyanpu shiyou yo. yakusoku wa mamoru tte itta desho?
lines.ja: じゃあさ、うちでキャンプしようよ。約束は守るって言ったでしょ？
lines.kana: じゃあさ、うちできゃんぷしようよ。やくそくはまもるっていったでしょ？
lines.english: Then let's camp at home. I said I'd keep my promise, didn't I?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uchi de? ii kedo, keikaku wa?
lines.ja: うちで？いいけど、計画は？
lines.kana: うちで？いいけど、けいかくは？
lines.english: At home? Sure, but what's the plan?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: keikaku wa boku ga tateru. tento wa heya no naka. de, gohan wa kenta ga tsukuru.
lines.ja: 計画は僕が立てる。テントは部屋の中。で、ご飯はケンタが作る。
lines.kana: けいかくはぼくがたてる。てんとはへやのなか。で、ごはんはけんたがつくる。
lines.english: I'll work out the plan. The tent goes indoors. And you do the cooking.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora ga keikaku tateru to, kekkyoku boku ga gohan tsukuru n da.
lines.ja: ソラが計画立てると、結局僕がご飯作るんだ。
lines.kana: そらがけいかくたてると、けっきょくぼくがごはんつくるんだ。
lines.english: So when Sora makes the plans, I end up doing the cooking anyway.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii jan. kenta no gohan, oishii shi.
lines.ja: いいじゃん。ケンタのご飯、おいしいし。
lines.kana: いいじゃん。けんたのごはん、おいしいし。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: wakatta, wakatta. jaa, taifuu ga kite mo, uchi no kyanpu wa chuushi ni naranai ne.
lines.ja: わかった、わかった。じゃあ、台風が来ても、うちのキャンプは中止にならないね。
lines.kana: わかった、わかった。じゃあ、たいふうがきても、うちのきゃんぷはちゅうしにならないね。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Well, at least our home camp won't get called off, even if the typhoon comes.

choices.english: Work comes up for Sora again, so Kenta calls off the camping trip and decides to cook at home instead.
A typhoon gets their camping trip called off, so Sora, who promised to come this time, suggests camping at home instead.
They hear a typhoon is coming, so they decide to wait until the morning before deciding whether to go camping.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta reminds Sora to keep his promise this time, and Sora swears he will. Line 4: a typhoon is coming. Line 9: an email from the campsite settles it, kyanpu chuushi ni natta. Line 12: Sora suggests uchi de kyanpu shiyou yo and reminds Kenta he said he'd keep his promise. A: work came up for Sora last time (line 2), not now, and Kenta isn't the one who calls it off. C: Kenta does suggest waiting until the morning (line 5), but the email arrives that same evening, so there's nothing left to wait for (line 10).

questions.english: Kenta says: "I think I might be getting a cold. Should I take tomorrow off work?" Tell him to wait and see how he feels for now before deciding.
questions.ja: なんか風邪ひいたかも。明日、仕事休んだほうがいいかな？
questions.kana: なんかかぜひいたかも。あした、しごとやすんだほうがいいかな？
questions.romaji: nanka kaze hiita kamo. ashita, shigoto yasunda hou ga ii kana?
questions.answer: Tell him to hold off and see how it goes with yousu o miru, not plain matsu: toriaezu konban wa yousu mitara?

modelAnswers.ja: とりあえず今晩は様子見たら？
modelAnswers.english: Why not just see how you feel tonight for now?

modelAnswers.romaji: mada wakannai yo. ashita no asa made yousu mite kara kimetara?
modelAnswers.ja: まだわかんないよ。明日の朝まで様子見てから決めたら？
modelAnswers.english: You can't tell yet. Why not wait and see till tomorrow morning, then decide?

questions.explanation: Holding off to see how something develops is yousu o miru, literally 'look at how things are'. Kenta says toriaezu ashita no asa made yousu miyou about the typhoon (line 5), and once the camp is off Sora says ashita made yousu miru hitsuyou mo nakatta ne (line 10). Plain matsu ('wait') says nothing about watching how things go. For a cold, friends and doctors alike say yousu o miru.

questions.english: What did Sora say about Sunday's football match?
questions.ja: ソラさんは日曜日のサッカーの試合について、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんはにちようびのさっかーのしあいについて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai ni tsuite, nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Apparently it's already been called off.

questions.explanation: Line 6: nichiyoubi no sakkaa no shiai, mou chuushi ni natta tte. A match, a festival or any other event that gets called off is chuushi ni naru, and the camping trip gets the same phrase in line 9. B, kyanseru sareta, is English 'cancelled' word for word. kyanseru is for bookings and your own arrangements, as in Kenta's yoyaku mo kyanseru shinakya (line 9), not for an event that gets called off. A, enki ni natta, is the same frame with a different outcome: put off to a later date, not called off.

questions.english: Yuki says: "You're really coming tomorrow at ten, right? Don't be late like last time." Tell her not to worry: this time you'll keep your promise.
questions.ja: 明日の十時、ほんとに来てくれる？前みたいに遅れないでね。
questions.kana: あしたのじゅうじ、ほんとにきてくれる？まえみたいにおくれないでね。
questions.romaji: ashita no juuji, honto ni kite kureru? mae mitai ni okurenaide ne.
questions.answer: Promise with yakusoku o mamoru, not motsu: daijoubu, kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamoru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: daijoubu, kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamoru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 大丈夫、今度はちゃんと約束守るよ。
modelAnswers.english: Don't worry, this time I'll keep my promise properly.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, yakusoku wa mamoru kara. juuji ni iku ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、約束は守るから。十時に行くね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'll keep my word. I'll be there at ten.

questions.explanation: Keeping a promise is yakusoku o mamoru, literally 'protect the promise'. Kenta reminds Sora with kondo wa chanto yakusoku mamotte yo (line 1), and Sora pledges yakusoku wa mamoru yo (line 2), then holds him to it: yakusoku wa mamoru tte itta desho? (line 12). English 'keep' points to motsu, but Japanese doesn't say that about promises. Since Yuki is worried about lateness, being on time takes the same verb: jikan o mamoru.

questions.english: For the camp at home, what does Sora say he'll do himself?
questions.ja: うちでキャンプするとき、ソラさんは何をすると言いましたか？
questions.kana: うちできゃんぷするとき、そらさんはなにをするといいましたか？
questions.romaji: uchi de kyanpu suru toki, sora-san wa nani o suru to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Work out the plan for it.
Put the tent up in the room.

questions.explanation: Line 14: keikaku wa boku ga tateru. Plans are 'stood up' in Japanese: keikaku o tateru is working out a plan, as Kenta says about his month of planning (sengetsu kara keikaku tateteta, line 3; sekkaku keikaku tateta noni, line 11). B: tateru literally means 'stand something up', and the tent comes up next (tento wa heya no naka), but Sora only says where it goes. The thing he's standing up is the plan. C: the cooking goes to Kenta (gohan wa kenta ga tsukuru), and Kenta notices: sora ga keikaku tateru to, kekkyoku boku ga gohan tsukuru n da (line 15). You tsukuru a meal but tateru a plan.

newWords.english: cancel (a booking, an order, your own plans)
